sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian often marks the possessor relationship directly on the possessed noun — either as a suffix attached to it, or as a stand-alone possessive pronoun built the same way.

items.english: His/her phone is on the table.

sections.content: Hungarian doesn't need a separate word for 'his' or 'her' the way English does — the possessor is folded straight into the noun's ending: telefon becomes telefonja. Once you know the possessive endings, you can mark 'my', 'your', 'his', 'our' and so on directly onto almost any noun.
